abstract_summary: LLM agents increasingly act as personal assistants that must remember a user's profile over months: who they are (attributes), what they routinely do (habits), and what they prefer (preferences), and keep it updated as jobs, routines, and tastes drift. scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The benchmark provides a well-motivated and rigorous setup for testing long-horizon agent memory across temporal checkpoints. The methodology includes detailed human validation of intermediate generated artifacts, and the evaluation features extensive ablation, error decomposition, and calibration of the LLM judge.

five quarterly checkpoints, exposing how performance scales with history length and
whether systems correctly overwrite superseded values as the profile evolves. To our knowledge,
DynamicMem is the most fine-grained long-horizon memory benchmark to date: about 2.2M tokens
per user over 15 months, 17,715 grounded events spanning 16 apps and 66 APIs, 1,837 evolving
attribute / habit / preference items linked by 383 causally-attributed state transitions, and 4,994 fine-
grained scoring points across 3,634 checkpoint-based problems. Benchmarking five representative
memory systems, we surface drawbacks that a single accuracy number hides. First, as the history
grows, State Completion accuracy falls steadily while Personalized Service does not, even though
both read the same memory. Second, no system both retains facts that stay true and overwrites facts

evidence.excerpt:
time, we can generate
more than one year long trajectories with over two million tokens per user without concatenating
irrelevant chat histories from other datasets. As shown in Figure 1, the pipeline is organized top-down
in three stages:(1) Multi-timescale user profile constructionproduces an evolving user profile;(2)
Intent-conditioned event chain generationwhich turns that profile into coherent multi-step intents; and
(3) State-consistent multi-app log generationwhich grounds each intent into concrete app interactions.
Each stage is conditioned on the output of the previous one, so every app log is traceable to the user
intent and profile state that produced it. We detail each stage below.

Figure 4, the judge returns two scores: CORE∈ {0,1}, indicating whether the prediction recovers the
central fact, and DETAIL∈ {0,1,2}, which measures how well it preserves the supporting specifics,
with 0, 1, and 2 corresponding to incorrect, partially correct, and fully correct details, respectively.
The final per-field score iss= 0.8·CORE+ 0.2·(DETAIL/2).

final score. Take the weekend-walk habit in Figure 4: the reference specifies the walk's frequency,
days, start/end time, and location. Suppose the prediction is"Saturday weekly walk at 06:35 by the
river"against the ground truth of"Saturday/Sunday weekly walk at 06:30–07:30, lakefront trail".
Frequency receives CORE=1 (weeklymatches); start

evidence.excerpt:
Baselines.We evaluate five memory systems:Vanilla RAG (RAG)[Lewis et al., 2021],Hip-
poRAG2[Gutiérrez et al., 2025],MemoryOS[Kang et al., 2025],A-Mem[Xu et al., 2025],Simple-
Mem[Liu et al., 2025]. We additionally report anOracleupper bound that is given the ground-truth
evidence required to complete each task item. We focus on query-agnostic memory systems that
pre-build a persistent per-user memory and then serve many downstream task items efficiently. For
all baselines, we use gpt-5-mini as the answer-generation LLM and text-embedding-3-large
for retrieval. Other experiment details are provided in Appendix I.

Finding 1.State Completion performance decreases as the horizon grows, whereas Personalized
Service performance remains stable and even improves slightly by leveraging the user's stateful
trajectory.
From C1 to C5, State Completion declines consistently across all memory systems. Compared
with C1, the C5 score drops by 4.4 points for RAG, 6.6 for HippoRAG2, 8.9 for A-Mem, 14.2 for
MemoryOS, and 16.7 for SimpleMem, as shown in Figure 5. Surprisingly, Personalized Service
shows no such degradation for four of the five systems: the C5 score is higher than the C1 score by

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: A manual human audit of 756 judge decisions found 96.3% agreement, and evidence retrieval recall independently corroborated the reported memory-bottleneck findings.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are produced by an LLM-as-a-judge scoring rubric against validated reference states, with supporting retrieval-recall and query-alignment measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evaluated memory systems are existing baselines run off-the-shelf with fixed memory construction and retrieval configurations; no system is trained, tuned, or selected on DynamicMem.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the degradation of profile reconstruction over long horizons, divergent behavior between service and state completion tasks, and retrieval bottlenecks causing >93% of failures are consistently backed by experimental data and stratified diagnostics.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The study benchmarks five existing memory architectures (Vanilla RAG, HippoRAG2, MemoryOS, A-Mem, SimpleMem) and an Oracle upper bound, complemented by temporal scalability tracking, retention vs. update trade-off analysis, evidence retrieval recall, and a precedence-based error classification.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Manual human audit of 756 judge decisions showed 96.3% agreement, and retrieval evidence recall directly corroborated failure patterns independently of the final answer generation model.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LLM-as-a-judge scoring with Core+Detail rubrics evaluated against validated reference states, supported by human agreement audits and retrieval recall measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: None directly tuned on the benchmark; existing baseline systems were evaluated off-the-shelf using fixed memory construction and retrieval configurations.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note that the synthetic dataset may not fully capture rare human behaviors and platform-specific idiosyncrasies found in real proprietary user logs, and evaluation relies on 10 seed personas.
primary.method_assessment: The construction pipeline generates evolving profiles across 6 life domains factorized into attributes, habits, and preferences, turns them into intent-driven event chains, and grounds them into state-consistent multi-app logs with structured schemas and stateful app tracking.
primary.quality_rationale: The benchmark provides a well-motivated and rigorous setup for testing long-horizon agent memory across temporal checkpoints. The methodology includes detailed human validation of intermediate generated artifacts, and the evaluation features extensive ablation, error decomposition, and calibration of the LLM judge.
primary.scoped_contribution: DynamicMem, a synthetic long-horizon benchmark evaluating memory-augmented LLM personal assistants across 15-month, 16-app grounded behavioral trajectories at five quarterly checkpoints via state completion and personalized service tasks.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The benchmark provides a well-motivated and rigorous setup for testing long-horizon agent memory across temporal checkpoints. The methodology includes detailed human validation of intermediate generated artifacts, and the evaluation features extensive ablation, error decomposition, and calibration of the LLM judge.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly note that the synthetic dataset may not fully capture rare human behaviors and platform-specific idiosyncrasies found in real proprietary user logs, and evaluation relies on 10 seed personas.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
